tasks.prompt: The three notes in notes/ come from different incidents. Turn what they have in common into a reusable pattern I can follow the next time a call with side effects might be retried, and check it against cases it should and shouldn't cover. Save the result to out/pattern.md.

assertions.text: The result compares all three notes in a table or equivalent structure with, per case, the context, the problem, the move that worked (or should have), and what failed when it was missing.
The result names one coordination axis that ties the cases together (e.g. making a side-effecting call safe to repeat when its outcome is unknown), not a broad theme such as 'reliability'.

The result names competing forces, including the duplicate-vs-lost-work tension from the first note (retrying duplicates labels; not retrying loses them), and at least one other cost such as key storage window, latency, or retry load.

The result gives ordered moves, each with a local check, covering: create the effect identity once when the intent is formed and before the first attempt; reuse the same identity on every repeat and reject it for a different payload; classify the outcome as succeeded, definitely failed, or unknown; on unknown, check status or repeat with the same identity instead of resending blindly; bound attempts.

The result shows what happens when a specific move is skipped, tied to the evidence (e.g. a key created per tap or per attempt produces duplicates; treating a timeout as FAILED leads to manual double payouts).

The result states when not to use the pattern or what to do instead, such as read-only or naturally idempotent calls, or a provider without idempotency support where status reconciliation is the only option.
The result runs the pattern on a case outside the notes' domains and shows the moves applied there.
The result states its evidence level and a falsifier or gap (e.g. only three synthetic cases from similar request/response settings).
out/pattern.md exists and can be followed without reading the notes.

tasks.notes: Uses the same notes as conceptualize/retry-notes. A good patternize result is executable (ordered moves with checks, skipped-move failures, boundary); a good conceptualize result is a single definition with transfer and boundary. If both skills' outputs pass each other's assertion sets at similar rates, that supports merging them. No-skill runs usually produce a generic 'retry with exponential backoff and idempotency keys' checklist without the unknown-outcome classification, the per-case evidence, or a boundary case.
